Lead Section:
The "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (The True Narcolist) is a series of five online videos that accused the Duterte family and allies of involvement in the illegal drug trade. Created by a man known as "Bikoy," the videos sparked controversy and legal actions. The series of videos, which were uploaded on April 2, 2019, named individuals and groups as part of a drug syndicate, including the mayor of Davao City, Bong Go, and the son of the president, Paolo Duterte. In a series of five online videos entitled the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (The real narco list), Bikoy - wearing a hooded sweatshirt to obscure his identity - claimed that drug money was funneled into the bank accounts of the mayor's brother and accused the Duterte family of being involved in the illegal drug trade.

Main Body:
On April 2, 2019, Peter Joemel Advincula, a former criminal, created a series of videos titled "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (transl. The True Narcolist) and uploaded them on YouTube. The videos alleged involvement of the Duterte family in the illegal drug trade and named individuals and groups as part of a drug syndicate, including the mayor of Davao City, Bong Go, and the son of the president, Paolo Duterte. The series of videos, which were uploaded on April 2, 2019, named individuals and groups as part of a drug syndicate, including the mayor of Davao City, Bong Go, and the son of the president, Paolo Duterte. The videos sparked a controversy and led to legal actions against the accused and the creator of the videos. The Philippine National Police (PNP) is now looking for the man behind the viral "Totoong Narco List" video accusing the Duterte family of being involved in the illegal drug trade.

1.content:
[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

On April 2, 2019, Peter Joemel Advincula, a former criminal, created a series of videos titled **"Ang Totoong Narcolist"** (transl. The True Narcolist). It discussed the alleged involvement of the [Duterte family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duterte_family "Duterte family") in drug syndicates, accusing politicians [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go") and [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), both closely related to the Duterte family. The videos garnered nationwide attention as politicians denied the accusations; a manhunt was also commenced.

During Advincula's childhood, he wanted to become a priest; he was introduced to a drug [syndicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicate "Syndicate"), which led to him being charged with [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") in 2012. Advincula had to remain in prison for six years; he was released one year early in 2017 due to [good character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_conduct_time "Good conduct time"). After dwelling in prison, Advincula wanted to become a [whistleblower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whistleblowing "Whistleblowing"). He created a channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" in YouTube on April 2, 2019, based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy". Five videos were produced, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6. The videos induced a manhunt for the perpetrator led by the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_(Philippines) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)"). Originally, Rodel Jayme, the owner of a website which distributed the videos, was apprehended on April 30. Just before Jayme was convicted, Advincula surrendered to the police. He paid his bail and left [Camp Crame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Crame "Camp Crame"), where he was detained, yet returned to the police for protection. Numerous politicians were charged with sedition, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo") and Trillanes. The [Oust Duterte matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix "Oust Duterte matrix"), a diagram exhibiting participants of an alleged ouster plot, was released on April 22, soon after the controversy.

Advincula was born in 1989, in [Donsol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donsol "Donsol"), Sorsogon, Philippines. He was introduced to a drug syndicate operating in [Misibis Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misibis_Bay "Misibis Bay") on May 6, 2010, and was selected to head [closed-circuit television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed-circuit_television "Closed-circuit television") operations in underground facilities throughout the area. After, he was tasked to prepare the monthly "TARA", a document listing the collections and payoffs that month.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) During this time, Advincula allegedly witnessed the killing of one of his syndicate members, as well as the raping of the latter's wife and daughter.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020133-2)

[![Image 2: Refer to caption](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_(cropped).jpg)

A portrait of President Rodrigo Duterte

Advincula fled the syndicate due to a fear that he would be murdered. Eventually, [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_(Philippines) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) agents found Advincula. He attempted to run from them but was arrested, convicted of fraud in 2012, and sentenced to six years in prison. During the first three years, he was detained at the [Naga City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naga,_Camarines_Sur "Naga, Camarines Sur") District Jail. He was transferred to the [New Bilibid Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Bilibid_Prison "New Bilibid Prison") due to good behavior. In prison, he returned to his religious activities, serving as a "teacher" for the local detainees.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) Allegedly, during his detainment, he contacted the office of Senator [Tito Sotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tito_Sotto "Tito Sotto"). He attempted to expose the businessmen who connected him to the drug syndicate to leave the prison. Sotto did not reply, finding his claims "suspicious."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He was released in 2017, one year early due to good character.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1)

### Duterte administration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Duterte administration")]

Rodrigo Duterte won the [2016 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election") and assumed presidency on June 30.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-4) His presidency was controversial and marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte%27s_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people under Duterte's command. This drew condemnation from the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and other international organizations.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-5) Large protests have also been held against the administration of Duterte; many of them were against the PNP killings.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-6) In September 2018, an alleged ouster plot, titled [Red October](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_October_(plot) "Red October (plot)"), was allegedly found, reportedly created by members of the opposition.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-7) In March 2019, Duterte exposed 46 "narcolists," or politicians with connections to drug syndicates.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-8) Along with this, various disinformation campaigns were created leading up to the [2019 Philippine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Philippine_general_election "2019 Philippine general election").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-9)[Surigao del Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surigao_del_Norte "Surigao del Norte") Representative [Ace Barbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_Barbers "Ace Barbers") portrayed these scandals as a possible motive for the creation of the "Bikoy" videos.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-10)

[![Image 3: A hooded figure staring in a black background](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/67/Bikoyvideostill.jpg/250px-Bikoyvideostill.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bikoyvideostill.jpg)

Still from _[The Philippine Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Philippine\_Star "The Philippine Star")_ showing the hooded figure in an episode of the "Bikoy" series

In August 2018, Advincula planned to go into hiding and become a whistleblower; he wanted to expose the Misibis Bay syndicate's operations.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) He created a YouTube channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (transl. The True Narcolist), set up on April 2, 2019. The videos are based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy", who claimed to be a former member of drug syndicates in [Southern Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Luzon "Southern Luzon") and the [Visayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visayas "Visayas") archipelago. According to _[Vera Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera\_Files "Vera Files")_, the videos seemed professionally done and had nice annotation.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) Five videos were created in total, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6; the videos were widely circulated throughout social media.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

The first episode was released on April 2.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) It displayed papers that "Bikoy" claimed to be TARA documents related to the syndicate. According to "Bikoy", typical TARA documents contain a date, a code name and bank account of a high-ranking official, and deposits made. The bottom of the documents flaunted a signature which ensured that the details in the documents were accurate. "Bikoy" then presented two code names, saying that the code names were not "so bright" due to their similarity to criminals' real names. He claimed the first code name was associated with Waldo Carpio, the brother of [Sara Duterte's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") husband, [Mans Carpio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mans_Carpio "Mans Carpio").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-14) He then purported that the other code name belonged to [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), alleging that the latter had a tattoo on his back showing the code name.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15)

The second episode was released five days later[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) through [Bombo Radyo Iloilo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombo_Radyo_Iloilo "Bombo Radyo Iloilo"). It divulged a new code name, which according to "Bikoy", was difficult to trace. He eventually associated the names to three bank accounts, including one belonging to Elijah Manuel Pepito and another to Veronica Salvador. Pepito was the partner lawyer for Mans Carpio's law firm. "Veronica Salvador" was a merged name of Duterte's wife, [Honeylet "Salvador" Avanceña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña"), and their daughter Kitty, shown as "Veronica".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-16)

The third episode was released on April 8, the following day,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-17) It discussed the alleged involvement of Senator [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go") in the drug trade. "Bikoy" claimed that drug money was being funneled to Go's account and insisted that Go had a dragon tattoo on his back with his code name.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) The fourth episode was released on April 12, four days later.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) In the video, "Bikoy" further argued that Go had a dragon tattoo and stated that he was confident of his allegation; he showed a picture of Go playing basketball with a portion of the dragon tattoo visible. In the video, he reiterated that Carpio was involved in drug operations.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-19) The fifth and final video was released on April 22. In it, "Bikoy" revealed alleged organizations related to the Misibis Bay syndicate and identified personalities he claimed were involved. He also exhibited the "Quadrangle Group", an alleged group of rich businessmen allegedly involved in drug operations.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)

Numerous Duterte-aligned politicians opposed the videos. During the episodes' release, [Presidential Spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_spokesperson_(Philippines) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)")[Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") said that the allegations mentioned were "[black propaganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_propaganda "Black propaganda")" and that "Bikoy" was just a "pawn." He also accused the [Liberal Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(Philippines) "Liberal Party (Philippines)") of creating the videos.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-20) After the first video, President Duterte blamed the political opposition and hinted that Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") was likely behind it, calling him [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-21) Due to Advincula's allegations that Bong Go has a dragon tattoo, Go has shown his back on two occasions: at a [Hugpong ng Pagbabago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugpong_ng_Pagbabago "Hugpong ng Pagbabago") campaign event[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) and later at a [Luntiang Pilipinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luntiang_Pilipinas "Luntiang Pilipinas") campaign event in [Calamba, Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamba,_Laguna "Calamba, Laguna").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-22) Trillanes praised the videos, wishing to have been part of the videos' creation. He then challenged [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte") to display the tattoo on his back, which Duterte refused to do.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15) The Liberal Party denied their involvement[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-23) while [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines") founder [Jose Maria Sison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Maria_Sison "Jose Maria Sison") said "Bikoy" should be given protection to tell his story.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-24) The [Department of Justice of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Justice_(Philippines) "Department of Justice (Philippines)") (DOJ) questioned "Bikoy"'s credibility due to his anonymity.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-25) The videos were considered a controversial topic online: viewers shared documents from the video, with a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") page titled "for the motherland Sass Rogando Sasot" encountering connections between the documents shown to a bank in [Legazpi, Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legazpi,_Albay "Legazpi, Albay").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-26) According to the [Philippine News Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_News_Agency "Philippine News Agency"), the videos were "publicly viewed, shared and uploaded" multiple times.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

### Oust Duterte matrix

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Oust Duterte matrix")]

Shortly after the release of the videos, specifically on April 16, Duterte reported in a speech that he had received intelligence reports detailing an alleged ouster plot. Six days later, Panelo released the "Oust Duterte matrix," on the president's orders. The matrix named journalists from several news outlets, particularly the [Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") and _[Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler")_. Panelo said those journalists could be feeding their stories to "enemies of the state," or the opposition. He stated that the matrix was released to expose those behind the alleged ouster plot and did not file charges against the journalists shown in the matrix.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-27)

Manhunt and investigation
-------------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Manhunt and investigation")]

### Rodel Jayme's arrest

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Rodel Jayme's arrest")]

The DOJ began investigating the videos April 17.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) The cybercrime division of the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_(Philippines) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) said that the website "metrobalita.net", a page which shared the videos, was owned by blogger Rodel Jayme. He was arrested in his residence in [Parañaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque") April 30 and detained in NBI headquarters.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:4-29) Jayme was them charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition") on May 2, with DOJ Secretary [Menardo Guevarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menardo_Guevarra "Menardo Guevarra") saying he could also be charged with child abuse for mentioning Duterte's daughter in one of the videos.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) Jayme accused opposition groups of forcing him to create the websites. An NBI spokesperson said that Jayme could be a state witness for the accusations.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-30)

### Peter Advincula's arrest

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Peter Advincula's arrest")]

Just before Jayme was to be charged, Peter Advincula, the original "Bikoy", emerged. He requested help from the [Integrated Bar of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Bar_of_the_Philippines "Integrated Bar of the Philippines") (IBP) in suing the Dutertes and their allies,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-31) maintaining his allegations were true. Two days later, the IBP rejected his offer. He then asked Senator [Panfilo Lacson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panfilo_Lacson "Panfilo Lacson") to postpone his hearing until the elections.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-32) That same day, Guevarra gave Advincula an ultimatum: bring evidence to back up his claims in the videos to the NBI, or face sedition charges.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-33) Advincula surrendered to police May 22, stating on national television that he played a role in a script made by the Liberal Party.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020132-36) The media called this reversal "[flip-flopping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip-flop_(politics) "Flip-flop (politics)")".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He also accused Trillanes of taking part in the video's production.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-37) The DOJ said that his allegations would need a deep investigation.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-38)[Solicitor General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_the_Philippines "Solicitor General of the Philippines")[Jose Calida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Calida "Jose Calida") offered legal aid to Advincula.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-39) Advincula had his [mugshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mug_shot "Mug shot") on May 23.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-40)[Elizaldy Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizaldy_Co "Elizaldy Co"), one of the people mentioned in the videos, filed a 1 billion PHP lawsuit for damage from the accusations relating to him.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-41)

The next day, Advincula, charged with for six counts of [estafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud"), paid 6,000 [PHP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_peso "Philippine peso") in bail.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-42) The next day, he left Camp Crame, where he was detained.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-43) The [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) started an investigation against Advincula[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-44) yet skipped a case hearing on the investigation the following day.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-45) He turned himself in to the police for protection on June 3, claiming that his life was in danger.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-46) The next day, the DOJ concluded their investigation, charging him with fraud, without a statement from Advincula.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-47) Trillanes released texts from Advincula for the production of the videos.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-48) Advincula was released from protective custody on June 25.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-49)[Ako Bicol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ako_Bicol "Ako Bicol") Representative [Alfredo Garbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Garbin "Alfredo Garbin") filed a resolution on May 29 for the [Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_House_Committee_on_Information_and_Communications_Technology "Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology") to investigate the potential effects of misinformation on social media platforms due to the videos.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12) The resolution resulted in investigations against Facebook and Google and a request for both to attend the hearing.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-50)

Numerous politicians were sued for sedition on July 18, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-51) Investigations began into his and other politicians' connection to the "Bikoy" videos.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-52) Advincula surrendered again to the PNP July 29.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-54) He posted 10,000 PHP bail two days later[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-55) and then applied for state protection on August 5 with his lawyer [Larry Gadon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Gadon "Larry Gadon").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-56) Two Catholic bishops were also charged with sedition later that month due to an alleged conversation with Advincula.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-57) On August 20, Calida linked the videos to servers in the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-58) Robredo responded to the investigations with a counter-affidavit, denying the accusations on August 29.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-59) In September, a former lawyer of Trillanes stated that the senator had ties to "Bikoy"; the senator denied the accusation.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-60) On February 10, 2020, Robredo was cleared of the charges against her, while [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") and actor [Joel Saracho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Saracho "Joel Saracho"), among others, were charged with sedition.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-61)

Aftermath and legacy
--------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Aftermath and legacy")]

On January 20, 2021, Advincula was charged with [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") by a Manila court for allegedly false statements against the [Free Legal Assistance Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Legal_Assistance_Group "Free Legal Assistance Group").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-63) A warrant was issued for his arrest.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-64) He surrendered at a local police station in [Daraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daraga "Daraga"), posting 18,000 PHP bail.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-65) He was absent from the court on July 21, causing the court to reissue his arrest warrant due to Advincula being unable to justify his absence.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-66) Advincula allegedly killed three politicians in [Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albay "Albay") on November 13, with their bodies appearing in his [ukay-ukay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukay-ukay "Ukay-ukay") store in Daraga. He was declared the primary suspect.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-68) According to local police, his possible motive was a grudge between him and one of the victims after the man rejected Advincula's request for a loan.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-69) He posted the 1 million PHP bail on December 16.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-70) Two years later, he was convicted of perjury in statements he made in 2019 implicating lawyers [Erin Tañada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_Ta%C3%B1ada "Erin Tañada"), [Chel Diokno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chel_Diokno "Chel Diokno"), and [Theodore Te](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Te "Theodore Te") in an ouster plot.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-72) He was sentenced to a maximum of one year and one day in prison.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-73) but eventually posted bail soon after the verdict.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-74) In 2020, a journal released by the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University") detailed the videos.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020126-75) On October 8, 2024, Advincula filed his candidacy for senator in the [2025 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philippine_Senate_election "2025 Philippine Senate election"), pushing for a centralized correctional system in the Philippines[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-77) but he was declared a [nuisance candidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuisance_candidate "Nuisance candidate") by the [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_(Philippines) "Commission on Elections (Philippines)").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-78)

Mission: Massacre the opposition
================================

[Philippine Daily Inquirer](https://opinion.inquirer.net/source/philippine-daily-inquirer) / 05:12 AM July 27, 2019

Share:

[![Image 26: Copy Link](https://opinion.inquirer.net/single2017/images/copy-link.svg)](https://opinion.inquirer.net/122886/mission-massacre-the-opposition#)

[![Image 28: image](blob:http://localhost/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)](https://opinion.inquirer.net/122886/mission-massacre-the-opposition#)

[![Image 30: Facebook](https://opinion.inquirer.net/single2017/images/fb-share.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fopinion.inquirer.net%2F122886%2Fmission-massacre-the-opposition)

[![Image 32: X](https://opinion.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fopinion.inquirer.net%2F122886%2Fmission-massacre-the-opposition)

From the very beginning, the series of viral videos under the umbrella title “Ang Totoong Narcolist” (“The Real Narcolist”), featuring a hooded figure under the alias “Bikoy,” had a suspicious stink about it.

For sure, the videos’ contents were explosive, purportedly revealing the real personalities behind the narcotics trade in the country, most prominently and shockingly including members of President Duterte’s family.

Authorities had an interesting reaction to the videos’ allegations. Instead of investigating the veracity of Bikoy’s claims, law enforcement set about seeking to unmask the hooded figure, initially arresting one Rodel Jayme who allegedly helped spread the videos through his website, MetroBalita. Then, one Peter Joemel Advincula came out, claiming he was Bikoy and appealing for help and protection from the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP). The Palace dismissed him forthwith as a serial liar—“You lie in one, you lie in all,” said presidential spokesperson Salvador Panelo—while the police tagged him as a wanted person for estafa and other crimes. In short, a con man.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

So it was a jaw-dropping moment when, days after Advincula failed to get the IBP’s backing for his allegations against members of the President’s family and official circle, the PNP trotted him out—now as their friendly witness. With police officialdom arrayed behind him at a press conference, Advincula proceeded to turn the tables on the alleged sponsors and makers of the video series, most prominently the political opposition.

FEATURED STORIES

OPINION

[Don't rush justice over Ex-Usec Bernardo's testimony](https://opinion.inquirer.net/188371/dont-rush-justice-over-ex-usec-bernardos-testimony)

OPINION

[Online scams and the elderly](https://opinion.inquirer.net/188361/online-scams-and-the-elderly-2)

OPINION

[The will to pass an anti-dynasty law](https://opinion.inquirer.net/188362/the-will-to-pass-an-anti-dynasty-law)

Advincula further stretched his 15 minutes of fame by signing an affidavit against those he claimed were behind the videos. Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group officials then used the affidavit to file a complaint of sedition and inciting to sedition against 36 individuals, among them Vice President Leni Robredo, now former senator Antonio Trillanes IV, several opposition figures and other individuals, including priests and bishops.

The complaint accused Advincula’s alleged financiers and supporters of “spreading lies against the President, his family and close associates, making them appear as illegal drug trade protectors and how they earned staggering amounts of money.” They also face charges of libel, cyberlibel, estafa, harboring a criminal and obstruction of justice.

Advincula’s lawyer, a gadfly who can be counted upon to make an appearance at every publicity-rich event, has claimed that the sedition charges could be the basis for the impeachment of Robredo.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

Now there’s a wrinkle in the otherwise seamless packaging of events. A report recently surfaced that, contrary to claims of Malacañang that it had nothing to do with the sedition charges, the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) had helped draft Advincula’s affidavit. The OSG in a statement said it was merely carrying out its “legal duty” to serve the state and its agencies when they seek legal advice.

Former Solicitor General and opposition senatorial candidate (and one of the 36 accused) Florin Hilbay begged to disagree. The OSG, he said, has no authority to assist in initiating the filing of criminal cases. The Solicitor General’s act of assisting the PNP in filing the charges lies beyond the scope of the OSG’s authority.

In criminal cases, Hilbay noted, the OSG enters the picture only in the appellate stage, once an accused who has been convicted appeals the conviction to the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court. Otherwise, there’s a conflict of interest, “because when you reach the appeal stage, the OSG’s hands are tied.”

_Article continues after this advertisement_

Certainly, the inciting to sedition case against the 36 accused fairly reeks of, if not conspiracy from the very top, then of impropriety from the President’s underlings. Former UP law dean Pacifico Agabin has said that while “there’s nothing illegal” in the OSG stepping into the case, it does not “look good on the part of the government.”

“It might not look good in the larger context, in the context of the position of the parties,” he explained. “Most of the respondents are all opposition figures, so it might be seen as an attempt to silence the opposition.”

It certainly looks like it. What the administration and its attack dogs are setting out on seems like an attempt at a wholesale massacre of the opposition. With the OSG’s grudging admission of having prepped him up, Bikoy’s stink now leads directly, indisputably, to Malacañang.

5.title: VERA FILES FACT CHECK: ‘Bikoy’ changes tune; implicates LP, Trillanes in ‘Ang Totoong Narco List’
5.description: In a 180-degree turn, Advincula who claims to be “Bikoy” implicated LP and Trillanes in the video series that linked members of the president’s family and his allies to the illegal drug trade.
5.content:
In a 180-degree turn, Peter Joemel Advincula who claims to be “Bikoy,” the hooded man in the “Ang Totoong Narco List” videos, now implicated the Liberal Party (LP) and Sen. Antonio Trillanes in the video series that linked members of the president’s family and his allies to the illegal drug trade.

From categorically stating he was “not connected” to any political party or affiliation, Advincula changed his story after being taken under police custody 17 days since his press briefing at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines.

**STATEMENT**

In a press briefing at the Philippine National Police, May 23, a day after he supposedly surrendered to authorities, Advincula said of the claims made in the video series:

> _“Hindi totoo ‘yun. Walang katotohanan lahat-lahat ‘yun_(They’re not true. There’s no truth to all of those)_. At ‘yoon pawang_ orchestrated _lamang ng mga nasa kabilang_ party (And [those claims] were only orchestrated by those in the opposition party)_,_ which is the Liberal Party under the handling of Senator Antonio “Sonny” Trillanes IV.”
> 
> 
> Source: PNP official Facebook page, NOW: Media briefing on the surrender of Peter Joemel Advincula, the confessed “Bikoy” character behind the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” video series, May 23, 2019, [watch](https://www.facebook.com/pnp.pio/videos/618971635248454/?t=446) from 7:28 to 7:47

**FLIP-FLOP**

This is the exact opposite of what Advincula said during a May 6 press briefing at the IBP, the first time he claimed he was Bikoy in the video series:

> “_Gusto kong linawin na wala akong kaugnayan sa kahit kaninong kandidato. Lalo na sa mga kandidato ng Otso Diretso, o anumang_ political party _o_ political affiliation.
> 
>  (I just want to clarify that I have no connection to any of the candidates. Especially to those of Otso Diretso, or any political party or affiliation.)”
> 
> 
> Source: ABS-CBN, Man behind viral anti-Duterte video surfaces, May 6, 2019, [watch](https://youtu.be/MX_zHFD5pgk?t=65) from 1:05 to 1:20

But in a May 23 statement, he insisted that he did not know Rodel Jayme, who was charged with inciting to sedition for allegedly uploading and sharing the controversial videos. Advincula also said he was not connected to and had “never even met” the media personalities in Malaca[ñ](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%C3%B1)ang’s matrix on the supposed destabilization plot against the government.

This is consistent with his statement where he said he had “no connection” to media personalities and institutions named in the matrix presented by Malaca[ñ](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%C3%B1)ang. The matrix, using the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” videos, lumped together some journalists, lawyers, and opposition figures in an alleged destabilization plot against the government.

Duterte administration hits back at claims president is involved in drug syndicate
==================================================================================

[![Image 1: Euan McKirdy](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/150103175015-euan-mckirdy-profile-new.jpg?c=16x9&q=h_270,w_480,c_fill/c_thumb,g_face,w_100,h_100)](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/euan-mckirdy)

 By [Euan McKirdy](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/euan-mckirdy), CNN 

 4 min read 

 Published 10:44 PM EDT, Tue May 7, 2019 

[](mailto:?subject=CNN%20content%20share&body=Check%20out%20this%20article%3A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.cnn.com%2F2019%2F05%2F07%2Fasia%2Fduterte-bikoy-philippines-unveiling-intl "Share with email")

 Link Copied! 

![Image 2: Davao City Vice Mayor Paolo Duterte, son of Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, and the president's son-in-law, Manases Carpio, take an oath as they attend a senate hearing in Manila on September 7, 2017.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/190507025016-paolo-duterte-01.jpg?q=x_4,y_251,h_2246,w_3991,c_crop/h_833,w_1480)

Davao City Vice Mayor Paolo Duterte, son of Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, and the president's son-in-law, Manases Carpio, take an oath as they attend a senate hearing in Manila on September 7, 2017.

Noel Celis/AFP/Getty Images

CNN—

Philippines President Rodrigo Duterte’s administration has strongly denied he has links to a drug syndicate, dismissing explosive allegations made by a man who went by the online pseudonym “Bikoy.”

In a series of five online videos entitled the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” (The real narco list), Bikoy – wearing a hooded sweatshirt to obscure his face – claimed to have documentary evidence that Duterte and his family members and close aides were deeply involved in the narcotics trade.

Duterte has waged a bloody and brutal war on drugs, which has seen thousands killed by police and vigilantes and which has sparked international condemnation.

Ad Feedback

Ad Feedback

As well as implicating the president, the man said the president’s son, the former Davao City vice mayor Paolo Duterte; former Special Assistant to the President Christopher “Bong” Go – now a senatorial candidate; and Duterte’s son-in-law, Manases Carpio – husband of Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte – were “players” in a drug syndicate.

All have denied any involvement with illegal drugs, with Go citing the president’s “hatred” of drugs as reason to stay away from the trade.

On Monday, the previously unidentified Bikoy allegedly outed himself as Peter Joemel Advincula, a heavyset man in his 20s or 30s with close-cropped hair and glasses.

Speaking at the offices for the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), the country’s national organization of lawyers, Advincula said his life was in danger after he implicated Duterte and those close to him.

Advincula claimed to have once been a part of the syndicate. Now wracked by guilt and hounded by death threats, he said he came forward to reveal his identity following the arrest of the webmaster of the site which first hosted the videos.

CNN has not been able to independently corroborate his claims that he is indeed the figure in the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” videos.

Politically sensitive timing
----------------------------

![Image 3: A poster of President Rodrigo Duterte's aide Bong Go is seen at an overpass as people take pictures of marching protesters during a rally at a road leading to Philippine Congress in Quezon City, east of Manila.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/190507025015-bong-go-01.jpg?q=w_1110,c_fill)

A poster of President Rodrigo Duterte's aide Bong Go is seen at an overpass as people take pictures of marching protesters during a rally at a road leading to Philippine Congress in Quezon City, east of Manila.

Richard James Mendoza/NurPhoto via Getty Images

The claims come just days before the country goes to the polls to elect lawmakers in mid-term elections. Their release has lit up social media in the Philippines, dividing opinion and sparking furious debate.

> > Are we in the verge of disclosing who are the real drug lords? [#Bikoy](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Bikoy?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)[#DuterteDrugSyndicate](https://twitter.com/hashtag/DuterteDrugSyndicate?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)[https://t.co/N3kIZhDMZf](https://t.co/N3kIZhDMZf)
> > 
> > — Gabrielle (@Gabgrielle) [May 6, 2019](https://twitter.com/Gabgrielle/status/1125293418110840833?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Government supporters say the allegations will backfire on opposition candidates. Others see the affair as spelling electoral disaster for candidates aligned with Malacanang, the presidential palace, and possibly criminal charges.

The chairman of the Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs, Panfilo Lacson, confirmed Tuesday that his panel would consider opening an investigation if Advincula provides a sworn statement. He added that compelling evidence must also be presented.

![Image 4: Supporters seen holding huge photos of opposition candidates.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/190507030039-otso-diretso-candidates-01.jpg?q=w_1110,c_fill)

Supporters seen holding huge photos of opposition candidates.

Josefiel Rivera/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images

In the videos, a hooded Bikoy said he used to work as an accountant for the syndicate operating in the southern Luzon and Visayas regions, “involved in recording transactions – how much money is allotted monthly per leader in the syndicate.”

He said he has complete records of these disbursements going back to 2010.

Advincula, speaking from the IBP, where he is seeking legal assistance and protection, said he decided to unmask himself because his past was gnawing at his conscience.

“I see the destruction of families due to drugs, of which I was once a part as a member of the syndicate. It is time to end the reign of this syndicate,” he said, according to [a translation from CNN affiliate](http://cnnphilippines.com/news/2019/5/6/Bikoy-reveal-identity.html) CNN Philippines.

‘Black propaganda’
------------------

Presidential spokesman Salvador Panelo described Bikoy’s claims as “black propaganda,” the official Philippines News Agency said, and dismissed the claims of the man on the grounds of his alleged past criminality.

“Information about the criminal background of Advincula is starting to come out. It appears that he has been incarcerated in 2012 for conviction of illegal recruitment and large scale estafa (fraud), as well as for theft,” the spokesman said in a statement Tuesday.

“Presently, there are news that he is facing multiple criminal cases like estafa, among others. These crimes involve moral turpitude that goes to the very integrity and credibility of Advincula or Bikoy,” he added.

In the videos, the man known as Bikoy claims to have indelible evidence. He alleges that Paolo Duterte has a tattoo which includes a code corresponding to his code name in the records – Alpha Tierra 0029.

Bikoy said Go, the senatorial candidate, also has a tattoo with a code which he has seen several times.

In response Go [showed his back publicly to prove he has no tattoo](http://cnnphilippines.com/news/2019/4/10/Bong-Go-drug-syndicate-dragon-back-tattoo.html). Panelo used the example as further evidence of Bikoy’s unreliability.

“There is a dictum in law which says: ‘You lie in one, you lie in all.’ This legal principle applies to Advincula or Bikoy,” the spokesman said.

So far Paolo Duterte has refused to show his back, CNN Philippines reports. He has admitted that he has a back tattoo, but has not confirmed or denied that it fits the description.

Panelo said there were “strong indications” that Advincula and Bikoy are the pawns of conspirators who seek to oust Duterte.

“Bikoy’s pretended fear for his life is part of the fraudulent act. Soon the pretenders and black propagandists will be unmasked,” the spokesman said.

9.title: Alias Bikoy’s Folly: Media Fail To Get at the Truth
9.content:
![Image 1: Three GMA news presenters are standing in front of a screen with an image of a man identified as Bikoy Kumambyo](https://cmfr-phil.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/GMA-News-YouTube_Alias-Bikoy%E2%80%99s-Folly-Media-Fail-To-Get-At-the-Truth-1024x598.png)

 Screen shot from _24 Oras’_ May 23 episode| GMA News YouTube[page](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bR6ptTHGSkE)

SEVENTEEN DAYS was all it took for Peter Joemel Advincula, alias “Bikoy,” the hooded figure in the controversial “_Ang Totoong Narcolist_” videos, to recant his statements about the involvement of the Duterte family in the drug trade.

In a press conference at the Philippine National Police (PNP) headquarters in Camp Crame on May 23, Advincula said all the allegations he made in the video were lies and claimed that the videos were part of a plot to oust the president by the Liberal Party (LP) and Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV. Media reports said Advincula surrendered to the PNP the previous night before because there were standing arrest warrants for his estafa cases.

Advincula first surfaced on May 6 at the office of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) when he sought legal assistance to sue the persons he had tagged as involved in the illegal drug trade. Those he named had immediately denied his accusations, with Malacañang describing the allegations as lies and black propaganda.

While the president and Palace officials kept claiming the existence of a plot to oust Duterte, they never provided evidence to prove it. After “Bikoy” videos surfaced beginning April 2, _The Manila Times_ on [April 22](https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/04/22/19/malacaang-claims-journalists-lawyers-behind-oust-duterte-plot) published a matrix linking critics, including a lawyers’ group, news organizations and journalists to an ouster plot along with the distribution of the Bikoy videos. Presidential Spokesperson Salvador Panelo said that Malacañang had the same information but the _Times_ preempted them in publicizing it.

On [May 8](https://www.rappler.com/nation/229986-malacanang-releases-new-diagrams-conspiracy-discredit-duterte-may-8-2019), Panelo and Presidential Communications Secretary Martin Andanar presented diagrams supposedly listing the wide network of conspirators. The expanded matrices included the LP, some members of the opposition and other groups.

But when Advincula went to the IBP, he denied having any connection with political parties and the media personalities previously tagged in the matrix.

The dots on the conspiracy no longer connected.

The media were quick to pick up Advincula’s statements recanting his claims, noting his change of tune. But media made no effort to make sense of the development, leaving this latest flip-flop to the public to take as they please. Although some reports expressed some reservations, most merely quoted his statements.

CMFR monitored the leading Manila broadsheets _Manila Bulletin_, _Philippine Daily Inquirer_ and _The Philippine Star_, the primetime newscasts (ABS-CBN 2’s _TV Patrol_, CNN Philippines’ _News Night_, GMA-7’s _24 Oras_ and TV5’s _Aksyon_), as well as selected news websites from May 23 to 30, 2019.

**“Bikoy” flip-flop**

Advincula’s flip-flop provoked some pointed observations from some of the media.

A report in [_24 Oras_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bR6ptTHGSkE)on May 23 included an observation by reporter Lei Alviz: “_Yan na ang linya ngayon ng nagpakilalang si Bikoy sa kumalat na ‘Ang Totoong Narcolist’ videos. Wala pang isang buwan mula nang iugnay niya ang pamilya Duterte sa kalakaran ng droga sa bansa, binaliktad na ni Peter Joemel Advincula ang kanyang mga sinabi_.” The _Inquirer_’s banner story on May 24, meanwhile, read: “[Bikoy changes tune, says LP, Trillanes behind videos](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1122741/bikoy-changes-tune-on-videos).”

Background details filled out some media accounts.[_24 Oras_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=78BRa_q1WPo)on May 23 and the [_Inquirer_](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1114686/what-went-before-true-narcolist-video) on May 24 aired reports which focused solely on reviewing what had happened before Advincula retracted.

[_Philstar.com_](https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2019/05/23/1920297/shifting-narratives-bikoy-videos-according-peter-advincula) provided a timeline of events on May 23, which also noted the change of tune of Malacañang and the PNP. Malacañang had previously dismissed Advincula’s claims on the video, but now said his current allegations about the involvement of the LP and Trillanes should be investigated. It also included PNP Chief Oscar Albayalde’s view that Advincula was just exercising his right to free expression and that the PNP’s hosting his press conference was not a “political exercise.” _Philstar.com_ recalled that Albayalde in June 2018 said that the PNP would stop the practice of presenting suspects to the media – a subtle jab at what the PNP did to accommodate Advincula.

Unfortunately, there was little added value in the weekend coverage nor in the subsequent exchange of unsubstantiated allegations. The coverage did not try to uncover more about Advincula’s person – who is the man, and where did he come from – being content instead with what little description was provided by the PNP.

**Is the ouster plot real?**

In an [interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N2fHZ1f0x0A) in GMA News’ online show “FYI with Richard Heydarian” on May 28, Defense Sec. Delfin Lorenzana said military and police intelligence have not found any “active threat” aimed at unseating Duterte, adding that destabilization efforts would require recruiting “a lot of people”, such as local officials, the police and the military.

The remark [prompted](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1124843/oust-duterte-plot-exists-only-its-not-credible-says-palace) Panelo to try to save face, since he had been talking about an oust-Duterte plot for weeks after the conspiracy matrix was published. Panelo who accompanied the president to attend the 25 th Nikkei Conference on the Future of Asia told reporters in Tokyo that there was no “inconsistency” between Malacañang’s position and Lorenzana’s statement. He claimed the defense chief merely meant that “the plot was not capable of being successful” and didn’t mean to say that there was no ouster plot against Duterte. It was a rare case of the presidential spokesperson interpreting what a senior Cabinet member was saying, without the media noting how Lorenzana’s statement clashed with those of Panelo who had been insisting the plot was real because the information came from Duterte himself.

Such conflicting statements on the ouster allegations showed up how the public has been taken for a ride wild claims from dubious personalities like Advincula, as well as Malacañang itself.

Speculation has been rife about who has masterminded what is obviously a hoax. But there has been little effort on the part of the media to get to the bottom of the issue. The mainstream media has appeared quite willing to carry the Palace spin on Advincula and his allegations as well as other serious matters.

Media seem to have become risk-averse about digging deeper to find the truth.

10.title: Alleged ouster plots against Rodrigo Duterte
10.content:
[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Since the win of President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") in the [2016 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election"), his [presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte") has been marked with controversy due to his crackdown on drugs and conflicts with organizations. Because of this, two attempts were allegedly made to oust him, namely the [Red October plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_October_(plot) "Red October (plot)") and the [Ang Totoong Narcolist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist "Ang Totoong Narcolist") videos. In response to the Ang Totoong Narcolist, a [matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix "Oust Duterte matrix") was made allegedly listing the figures wanting to oust Duterte.

The Red October plot was an alleged plot reportedly uncovered by Duterte on September 8, 2018. The numerous oppositions targeted said that the plot was fake. A [Chinese person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_people "Chinese people") was arrested on September 27 in [Teresa, Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teresa,_Rizal "Teresa, Rizal"), while schools were targeted for alleged participation in the plot. Next year, a former member of a drug syndicate created a YouTube channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" and uploaded five videos criticizing Duterte and his allies. The videos caused major controversy, leading the member of the drug syndicate and an opposition politician to be charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition").

Shortly after the YouTube channel made controversy, the Oust Duterte matrix was revealed by [Presidential Spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_spokesperson_(Philippines) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)")[Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo"), targeting politicians and journalists who allegedly took part in an "ouster plot" against Duterte. Numerous figures included in the matrix denied their participation.

In an interview with [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler") in the late months of 2015, Duterte announced his candidacy for president in the upcoming 2016 Philippine presidential election.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-1) He filed his Certificate of Candidacy for the presidential election a few days later, withdrawing from the mayoral race of [Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-2) After intense competition, he won with a total vote count of 16.6 million.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-3) His presidency was controversial, with his presidency marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte%27s_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people while carrying out thousands of raids. Because of this, he was involved in controversy against the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and other organizations.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-4)

In Davao City, Duterte accused the opposition of creating an ouster plot on September 8, 2018, with opposition stating that he was a victim of his own "paranoia".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:0-5) A protest was planned during this time, but nothing happened in the supposed protest areas.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:0-5) Duterte accused soldiers of holding discussions with rebel groups like the [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines") (CPP) and the [New People's Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_People%27s_Army "New People's Army") to oust him from office on September 24 in a military camp in [Jolo, Sulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolo,_Sulu "Jolo, Sulu"). The plot was allegedly named "Red October". The [Malacañang Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace"), the workplace of the president, released a video of his statement the next day.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-7) The day after that, the CPP said that the ouster plot was fake.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-8) Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo") stated that linking political opposition to ouster plots was a tactic used in [martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_under_Ferdinand_Marcos "Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos") to silence the opposition.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-9) Senator Antonio Trillanes denied his involvement in the ouster plot.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-10) Four days later, the military seized from 13 alleged members of the CPP which had laptops and documents that Gen. [Antonio Parlade Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Parlade_Jr. "Antonio Parlade Jr.") alleged to be proof of the ouster plot.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-11) The Makabayan denied their involvement on September 27, although they were planning for a protest rally the next month.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-ro0622-12)

A Chinese person was arrested on September 27 in [Teresa, Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teresa,_Rizal "Teresa, Rizal"). The PNP raided her house and found firearms. Her house was allegedly used as a hideout for communist [guerillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerillas "Guerillas"). Some allegations were made that, during the arrest, the national bribed the officers with "protection money" so that she would not be arrested.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-13) A list of schools across [Metro Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Manila "Metro Manila") which were allegedly involved in the plot was released on October 4 by the AFP, with the military stating that the CPP was trying to "brainwash the students" into taking part in the activities. Among the list provided were the [University of the Philippines Diliman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Philippines_Diliman "University of the Philippines Diliman"), the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University"), the [De La Salle University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_La_Salle_University "De La Salle University"), and the [University of Santo Tomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Santo_Tomas "University of Santo Tomas").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-14) The [Department of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Transportation_(Philippines) "Department of Transportation (Philippines)") said on October 7 that transport strikes were related to the plot. Department of Defense Secretary [Delfin Lorenzana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delfin_Lorenzana "Delfin Lorenzana") said on October 12 that the plot fell apart. The military said that the plot would be moved to December, the 50th founding anniversary of CPP, although CPP President [Jose Maria Sison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Maria_Sison "Jose Maria Sison") denied these claims. The same month, nine farmers were killed in the [Sagay massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagay_massacre "Sagay massacre"), which authorities claimed was related to the plot.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:0-5)

Peter Joemel Advincula was born on March 22, 1989, in [Donsol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donsol "Donsol"), [Sorsogon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorsogon "Sorsogon"). His mother was a parish secretary while his father was a farmer. He pursued a degree in [philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy "Philosophy").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:02-15) His father died in 2009. On May 6 that same year, he was introduced to a drug [syndicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicate "Syndicate") operating out of [Misibis Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misibis_Bay "Misibis Bay"). He was tasked to prepare the monthly "TARA", a document listing the collections and payoffs that month. He was convicted of [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") in 2012 and sentenced to six years in prison. He was released in 2017, one year early because of [good character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_conduct_time "Good conduct time").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:02-15) Wanting to become a [whistleblower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whistleblower "Whistleblower"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:02-15) he created a [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (transl. The True Narcolist) based around a former criminal named "Bikoy".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:1-16) Five videos were created in total, between April 2, 2019, and Advincula's surrender on May 6.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-17) The videos accused Duterte-aligned figures, including Waldo Carpio, the brother of [Sara Duterte's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") husband, [Mans Carpio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mans_Carpio "Mans Carpio"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:1-16)[Honeylet Avanceña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña") and her daughter Kitty Duterte,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-18) and [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:2-19) Duterte-aligned politicians including [Presidential Spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_spokesperson_(Philippines) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)")[Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") and Bong Go called the allegations false.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-21) Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") supported the videos.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-22) The [Liberal Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(Philippines) "Liberal Party (Philippines)"), a part of the opposition, denied their involvement in the videos.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-23)

The DOJ started investigating the videos on April 17.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:5-24) Blogger Rodel Jayme was arrested in his residence in [Parañaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque") on April 30 for his alleged involvement in the videos.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:4-25) Jayme was charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition") on May 2.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:5-24) Peter Advincula, the original 'Bikoy', surfaced on May 6. He asked for help from the [Integrated Bar of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Bar_of_the_Philippines "Integrated Bar of the Philippines") (IBP) to sue the Dutertes and their allies.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-26) The IBP rejected his offer.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-27) Advincula surrendered to police on May 23, stating that he played a role in a script made by the Liberal Party.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-28) The [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) started an investigation against Advincula on May 27.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-29) He turned himself in to the police for protection on June 3, suspecting that his life is in danger.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-30) The DOJ charged him with [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-31) He was released from protective custody on June 25.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-32) Politicians were sued for sedition on July 18, including Vice President Leni Robredo.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-33) Investigations were made into Robredo and other politicians' relation to the Bikoy videos.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-34) Advincula surrendered again to PNP on July 29.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-35) He posted the bail of 10,000 [PHP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_peso "Philippine peso") on July 31, getting released.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-36) Robredo responded to the investigation with a counter-affidavit, denying the accusations on August 29.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-37) On February 10, 2020, Robredo was cleared of her accusations while [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") was charged with On January 20, 2021, Advincula was charged with [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") by a Manila court for allegedly false statements against the [Free Legal Assistance Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Legal_Assistance_Group "Free Legal Assistance Group"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-39) surrendering in a local police station in [Daraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daraga "Daraga"), posting a 18,000 PHP bail.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-40) He allegedly killed three politicians in [Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albay "Albay") months later on November 13, with their bodies appearing in his _[ukay-ukay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukay-ukay "Ukay-ukay")_ store in Daraga. He was declared the primary suspect.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-41) He posted the 1 million PHP bail on December 16.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-42) In 2024, he filed his candidacy for senator in the [2025 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philippine_Senate_election "2025 Philippine Senate election") but was declared a [nuisance candidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuisance_candidate "Nuisance candidate") by the [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_(Philippines) "Commission on Elections (Philippines)").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-43)

"Oust Duterte" matrix
---------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: \"Oust Duterte\" matrix")]

After the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" YouTube channel caused controversy, a matrix was announced by Presidential Spokesperson Salvador Panelo on April 22. 2019. The matrix allegedly contained the names of journalists and organizations who want to oust Duterte, with journalists from the [Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") (PCIJ) and [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler"). Panelo said that there was a "basis to release it" and that the matrix underwent "proper validation".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-44) Another version of the matrix was released on May 8, with a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation to support the claims. The other version included "active online collaboration" between multiple opposition figures.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-45) Filipino Olympian [Hidilyn Diaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidilyn_Diaz "Hidilyn Diaz") was "shocked" over her inclusion in the matrix.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-46) Multiple major journalists claimed the matrix as "false". The PCIJ said the report was "wrong on many points". Rappler said that the report was an example of "how not to write an investigative report or even straight news."[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-47) Former journalists included in the matrix told the media about their inclusion.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-48) The National Union of Peoples' Lawyers asked the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") for government protection after harassment related to their involvement in the matrix.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-49) An editor for _[The Manila Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Manila\_Times "The Manila Times")_ resigned on April 26 because the early article was "poorly sourced", later stating in an interview that he was asked to resign from the newspaper.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-50)

In response to this, Duterte called the ambassadors "spies", although the United States government responded to the allegations as false.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-51) Paolo Duterte released a list on December 10, 2018, which contained people who allegedly wanted to oust Duterte including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo"), former government officials, and journalists. The [Malacañang Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace") defended Duterte's list stating that there is no need to probe it. "I know that the Armed Forces and the Police will have to decide one day somehow. _Philippine National Police chief Oscar Albayalde doubts the claims of the man called 'Bikoy,' saying his video seems 'self-serving' and that having a dragon tattoo doesn't prove anything_

MANILA, Philippines – The Philippine National Police (PNP) is now looking for the man behind the viral [“Totoong Narco List”](https://www.rappler.com/nation/227352-malacanang-dismisses-totoong-narco-list-video-black-propaganda)video accusing presidential son Paolo Duterte of receiving money from a crime syndicate and using the brother of his brother-in-law as a dummy for the transactions.

In response to reporters who asked if the PNP would trace the man, Albayalde said on Monday, April 15: “I think we’ll do that already…. As of this time, no one has come to us to complain, but we will do the initiative to identify this person.”

According to Albayalde, the man who calls himself “Bikoy” may have committed cyber libel for producing the video and posting it online.

“If he really has evidence, we can help him file a case against those he named. But if he doesn’t, then he will be made liable for all that he has said,” Albayalde added in a mix of English and Filipino.

The video shows “Bikoy” claiming that he worked for Philippine drug syndicates and handled transaction records. He shows documents indicating multimillion-peso bank transfers to accounts supposedly owned by[Paolo Duterte](https://www.rappler.com/nation/politics/elections/2019/227536-otso-diretso-dares-paolo-duterte-show-tattoo-clear-your-name) and Waldo Carpio, the brother of Sara Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio.

![Image 5: A DARE. Opposition election candidates have challenged former Davao City vice mayor Paolo Duterte to answer the allegations against him head-on. File photo by LeAnne Jazul/Rappler ](https://www.rappler.com/tachyon/r3-assets/612F469A6EA84F6BAE882D2B94A4B421/img/D4D10325C6F44356AEC705D2452EE405/paolo-duterte-manases-carpio-senate-september-6-2017-001_0f8d57e6a83d480095b9b5799c813003.jpg)

**What does the PNP think of the man’s claims?** At the end of the video, “Bikoy” claimed that Paolo Duterte bore a dragon tattoo on his back and that under the eye of this dragon is the code “Alpha Tierra 0029,” the same code name in the supposed “tara” or grease money.

Albayalde doesn’t buy these claims, saying that “you can always accuse anybody” and that the video appears to be “self-serving.”

The PNP chief added that [dragon tattoos](https://www.rappler.com/entertainment/news/181841-robin-padilla-dragon-tattoo-bureau-immigration) do not amount to anything in criminal investigation as they haven’t encountered any illicit organization using body ink to prove membership.

_“Marami kasing nagpapa-tattoo na gusto nila dragon eh. Alam mo ‘yung symbol of dragon, it’s authority, ‘yung tapang. ‘Yung virtue ng dragon, halos lahat tayo gusto natin ng dragon talaga eh. Otherwise, masama naman siguro kung butiki ipapa-tattoo ko,”_ Albayalde said.

(Many want a dragon tattoo. The dragon symbolizes authority, bravery. With the virtues of the dragon, all of us want to have a dragon tattoo. Otherwise, wouldn’t it be unappealing to get a lizard tattoo?)**– Rappler.com**
